solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Composer with worry over French region (8)

indicatorNotes.over: CARE is turned over, so it reads backwards

annotation.surface: A composer frets about some French region.
annotation.walkthrough: Bergerac is a wine area in the Dordogne of south-west France.
annotation.definitionFit: Bergerac is a town and wine region in south-west France.

entries.clue: Shelter soldiers from south capturing missile launcher (7)

indicatorNotes.from south: in a down answer, starting from the south means reading upwards, so REME runs backwards
indicatorNotes.capturing: to capture is to seize and hold, so EMER holds BOW prisoner inside it

blocks.note: REME = Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
container indicator: the reversed soldiers hold the bow between their letters

annotation.surface: Troops advancing from the south take a rocket launcher and dig in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Missile launcher' suggests modern weaponry, but it is the archer's bow.
annotation.definitionFit: To embower is to shelter or enclose, as in a bower of leaves.

entries.clue: Castle of the Groans — lead characters in magnificent gothic novel (11)

annotation.definition: Castle of the Groans — lead characters in magnificent gothic novel

blocks.note: 'Groans' reads as moaning, but the Groans are a family, the owners of a vast crumbling castle

blocks.clueFragment: lead characters in magnificent gothic novel
blocks.note: the Groan family, Titus above all, are the leading characters of Mervyn Peake's gothic novels, one of which is named after their castle

annotation.surface: A description of a sprawling gothic castle and the family at its heart.
annotation.walkthrough: GORMENGHAST is the castle of the Groans in Mervyn Peake's trilogy, and also the title of its second book; there is no wordplay to take apart.
annotation.definitionFit: Gormenghast is the vast castle ruled by the Groan family in Peake's trilogy.

entries.clue: Athenians for example denied their capital stinks (5)

indicatorNotes.denied their capital: GREEKS loses its capital, i.e. first, letter

annotation.surface: Athenians, stripped of their capital city, are left in a foul state.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital' tempts toward Athens the city; here it means the capital letter at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: Reeks means stinks: both are verbs for giving off a bad smell.

entries.clue: Ancient instrument — store it in cleaner area (7)

indicatorNotes.store: to store something is to keep it inside, so CHAR keeps IT within
indicatorNotes.in: IT sits in the cleaner, placed within her letters

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner in British English
IT as written, stored inside: C(IT)HAR

annotation.surface: A museum piece should be put away in a cleaner's cupboard.
annotation.walkthrough: A char is a British cleaning lady, short for charwoman.
annotation.definitionFit: The cithara was an ancient Greek lyre-like stringed instrument.

entries.clue: Ton added to gold in room a shock (6)

indicatorNotes.added to: a thing added to another is joined on, so T is joined to the front of the rest
indicatorNotes.in: gold is in the room, so AU sits within RM

blocks.note: RM = room, with AU inside: R(AU)M
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

annotation.surface: Finding a ton of gold in a room would be quite a shock.
annotation.walkthrough: RM is the standard abbreviation for room, as in small ads.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a shock severe enough to leave lasting damage is a trauma.

entries.clue: Swirling dry northerly heading for Urals fast (9)

indicatorNotes.northerly: in a down answer, going north means reading upwards, so BRUT runs backwards
indicatorNotes.heading for: take the head, the first letter, of Urals

blocks.note: Lent is the Christian fast before Easter

annotation.surface: A weather report: a dry north wind swirling rapidly toward the Urals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like speed, but it is Lent, the season of fasting.
annotation.definitionFit: Turbulent air or water is swirling and disturbed.

entries.clue: Old Islamic leader calls in periodically (3)

indicatorNotes.periodically: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so take letters at regular intervals: every second one
indicatorNotes.in: the letters are found in the words 'calls in', not elsewhere

blocks.note: the even letters of cAlLs In

annotation.surface: A former Islamic leader drops by from time to time.
annotation.walkthrough: Ali, cousin and son-in-law of Muhammad, was the fourth caliph.
annotation.definitionFit: Ali ibn Abi Talib was an early caliph, a leader of Islam in the seventh century.

entries.clue: Kit the writer debased in unpleasant experience (7)

indicatorNotes.in: debased sits in the unpleasant experience, so LOW goes within MARE

blocks.note: a mare, short for nightmare, is British slang for an awful experience; LOW sits between its R and E

annotation.surface: A writer's equipment has been cheapened by some nasty episode.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kit' looks like equipment but is Christopher Marlowe's nickname; 'a mare' is British slang for a nightmare of a time.
annotation.definitionFit: Christopher 'Kit' Marlowe was the Elizabethan playwright of Doctor Faustus.

entries.clue: Bishop and religious fraternity row about stray dog (6,7)

indicatorNotes.about: about means surrounding, so the row goes round the stray: TIER encloses ERR

blocks.note: a religious order, such as the Franciscans
a tier is a row of seats; it goes around ERR: T(ERR)IER

annotation.surface: A bishop and a monastic brotherhood quarrel over a stray dog.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel; it is a tier of seats.
annotation.definitionFit: The border terrier is a small rough-coated terrier breed.

entries.clue: Ship carrying blubber passes swiftly (6)

indicatorNotes.carrying: a ship carrying cargo holds it inside, so SS holds WEEP

blocks.note: SS = steamship, a standard prefix; the crying goes between the two S's
to blubber is to weep noisily

annotation.surface: A whaling ship loaded with blubber speeds by.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blubber' sounds like whale fat on a ship, but it is the verb for crying.
annotation.definitionFit: Sweeps is a plain synonym here: a gust or car that sweeps by passes swiftly.

entries.clue: American descendant touring one foreign capital (8)

indicatorNotes.touring: to tour a place is to go all the way round it, so SCION goes round UN

blocks.note: a scion is a descendant; it goes around UN: S(UN)CION

annotation.surface: An American heir on a trip abroad visits a foreign capital.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' seems to describe the capital, but it belongs to 'one', which turns it into French UN.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Asunción is one capital city, the seat of government of Paraguay.

entries.clue: Scours harbour — having lost walrus? (5-6)

annotation.surface: Someone scrubs a harbour after a walrus has gone missing.
annotation.walkthrough: The walrus is a walrus moustache, the big droopy kind; the question mark flags the joke.
annotation.definitionFit: A man who has shaved off his walrus moustache is clean-shaven.

entries.clue: Robbing criminal barged in to bag silver (10)

indicatorNotes.criminal: the letters of BARGED IN are rearranged
indicatorNotes.to bag: the anagram holds AG inside it

blocks.note: anagram fodder, rearranged to BRIGAND…E around AG
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

annotation.surface: A robber forces his way in to make off with the silver.
annotation.walkthrough: Brigandage is the noun for highway robbery, so 'Robbing' works as a noun here.
annotation.definitionFit: Brigandage is robbery carried out by brigands; 'robbing' as a noun means the same.

entries.clue: Rodent warranty altered to protect duck (6,3)

indicatorNotes.altered: an altered document has been changed, so the letters of WARRANTY change order
indicatorNotes.to protect: to protect something is to surround and shield it, so the anagram surrounds O

blocks.note: anagram fodder, rearranged to N…RWAY RAT around O
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

annotation.surface: A pest-control warranty is amended so it covers ducks too.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, which looks like O.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Norway rat, better known as the brown rat, is one kind of rodent.

entries.clue: First couple expelled from country paradise (4)

indicatorNotes.First couple expelled from: the first couple of letters are thrown out of the word, so SW goes

blocks.note: Sweden, minus its first couple of letters SW

annotation.surface: The first couple are thrown out of paradise: Adam and Eve's expulsion.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is the Book of Genesis, with the answer in plain sight, but the 'first couple' are just two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Eden is the biblical garden of Genesis, and its name became a byword for any paradise.

entries.clue: Work always around for lauded artist (4)

indicatorNotes.around: to turn around is to face the other way, so AY is read backwards

blocks.note: ay (or aye) = always, an old word

annotation.surface: A plea to keep working to become a celebrated artist.
annotation.walkthrough: AY for 'always' is an archaic word, common in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya is a celebrated Spanish painter.

entries.clue: Old barrel brought into bar sounding full (7)

indicatorNotes.brought into: something brought into a place ends up inside it, so TUN goes inside ROD

blocks.note: a rod is a bar; TUN goes inside: RO(TUN)D
a tun is a large cask

annotation.surface: An old cask is carried into a pub that echoes loudly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bar' reads as a pub but is a rod; ROTUND itself hides in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An orotund voice is full, round and resonant.

entries.clue: Substantial cardinal sin brought about court action (4,6)

indicatorNotes.brought about: SIN is turned about, so it reads backwards

annotation.surface: A cardinal's grave sin has led to a lawsuit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman beside 'sin', but it is a cardinal number; 'court action' sounds legal but is sport.
annotation.definitionFit: Real tennis is the old indoor court game from which lawn tennis descends.

entries.clue: Stomach calmer in colonist, perhaps on powerful drug (7)

blocks.note: ANT sits on top of ACID in the down answer

annotation.surface: A settler who took a strong drug needs something to settle his stomach.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Colonist' suggests a settler; an ant is a member of a colony.
annotation.definitionFit: An antacid neutralises stomach acid, calming indigestion.

entries.clue: Dip in northwestern river curtailed after one minute (7)) (7)

indicatorNotes.curtailed: MERSEY loses its tail, the last letter
indicatorNotes.after: the river comes after I and M

blocks.note: the Mersey flows through Liverpool in north-west England
stray scraped text, not part of the clue

annotation.surface: A quick swim in a north-west river, just a minute's dip.
annotation.walkthrough: The Mersey is the river of Liverpool, in north-west England.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to dip an object in liquid and to immerse it both mean putting it under.

entries.clue: Reportedly deficient characteristic in vivid description (8)

indicatorNotes.Reportedly: as heard said, not as spelt

annotation.surface: A flaw in someone's character is exposed in a vivid account.
annotation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic British accent, 'poor trait' and 'portrait' match.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a portrait can be painted in words, a vivid description of a person.

entries.clue: Mental model found in Nietzsche, maybe (6)

indicatorNotes.found in: the answer is found inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A theory of mind that might turn up in Nietzsche's philosophy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' reads as hedging but is there only for its first two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: In psychology a schema is a mental model or framework for organising knowledge.

entries.clue: Glide across water with doubled force in boat (5)

indicatorNotes.doubled: doubled means made twofold, so the F for force appears twice

annotation.surface: Forcefully rowing a small boat so it seems to glide over the water.
annotation.walkthrough: F for force is the physics symbol.
annotation.definitionFit: A skiff is a light rowing or sailing boat.

entries.clue: Working to a Greek character always, who might do better? (13)

blocks.note: working to a boss = working under them

annotation.surface: A report on someone working towards a Greek letter: could do better.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Could do better' is the classic school-report phrase, which the definition echoes.
annotation.definitionFit: An underachiever performs below their ability, someone who might do better.

entries.clue: No power in bass for Flower of Scotland (3)

indicatorNotes.No power in: having no power in means lacking it, so the P for power is removed from DEEP

blocks.note: a bass voice is deep; drop P for power

annotation.surface: A bass singer runs out of steam during Scotland's anthem, Flower of Scotland.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'flower' is something that flows, a river; the Dee runs through Aberdeen. Flower of Scotland is also Scotland's unofficial anthem.
annotation.definitionFit: The Dee is a Scottish river, a 'flower' in the sense of something that flows.

entries.clue: Commercial to air in time prior to Christmas (6)

annotation.surface: Advertisements to be broadcast in the run-up to Christmas.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To air' suggests broadcasting a commercial, but it means to vent.
annotation.definitionFit: Advent is the season of the four weeks before Christmas.

entries.clue: Footballer put off allowing goal in (8)

indicatorNotes.allowing: allowing something in means letting it enter, so DEFER lets END inside
indicatorNotes.in: the goal goes in, within the letters of DEFER

blocks.note: to put off is to defer; the goal sits between its F and E
an end is a goal, an aim

annotation.surface: A footballer is dropped for letting a goal in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Goal' looks like football, but it is END, an aim.
annotation.definitionFit: A defender is a footballer whose job is to stop the other side scoring.
